rv.q: One extremely slick attraction, A Ghost in Your Ear is a yummy piece of Halloween candy aimed for date nights and families with teens, because it’s ultimately an entertaining horror show where not a dirty word is ever heard.
This is a performance that demands to be both heard and seen.
It's a disorienting sensation, but one that enhances this slice of ASMR horror.
A Ghost In Your Ear combines effective sound design with classic horror tropes — a haunted manor, a debilitating storm, a dark past — to create a truly unique experience on stage.
For all its theatrical ingenuity, however, the show is ultimately more impressive for its technical rather than thematical elements.
All of the scares — and I could count them on exactly one hand — are visual.
A Ghost in Your Ear is a rare theatrical treat.
Even so, for those who enjoy being spooked, A Ghost in Your Ear sets a high bar for immersive theatrical storytelling.
If the frights are milder than one might hope, the work surprisingly has something to say about the travails of fatherhood.

cn.t: Critics mostly praise this binaural ghost story's innovative use of immersive headphone technology to deliver intimate scares, though some find the gimmick overshadows substance. A distinctive Halloween treat that's unlike anything else on New York stages.

vr.q: I was bored by the story within the story. It just it wasn't that interesting of a ghost story to me.
